exposure: Mode of diabetes treatment (diet therapy, insulin therapy)
outcome: Clinical management (mode of treatment, glycemic control, HbA1c, glycemia)
Pregnancy outcomes (miscarriages, neonatal hypoglycemia, maternal and neonatal outcomes)
cohort: The study included 36 pregnancies from 27 patients diagnosed with monogenic diabetes, specifically GCK-hyperglycemia (14 patients, 18 pregnancies) and HNF1A-MD (13 patients, 18 pregnancies).
finding: Pregnancy outcomes in patients with GCK-hyperglycemia and HNF1A-MD monogenic diabetes were comparable and generally favorable, with individualized insulin therapy and regular monitoring supporting safe management.
